better-auth-best-practices\\\\\\\\ndescription: Skill for integrating Better Auth - the comprehensive TypeScript authentication framework.\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n# Better Auth Integration Guide\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Always consult [better-auth.com/docs](https://better-auth.com/docs) for code examples and latest API.**\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nBetter Auth is a TypeScript-first, framework-agnostic auth framework supporting email/password, OAuth, magic links, passkeys, and more via plugins.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Quick Reference\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Environment Variables\\\\\\\\n- &#96;BETTER_AUTH_SECRET&#96; - Encryption secret (min 32 chars). Generate: &#96;openssl rand -base64 32&#96;\\\\\\\\n- &#96;BETTER_AUTH_URL&#96; - Base URL (e.g., &#96;https://example.com&#96;)\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nOnly define &#96;baseURL&#96;/&#96;secret&#96; in config if env vars are NOT set.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### File Location\\\\\\\\nCLI looks for &#96;auth.ts&#96; in: &#96;./&#96;, &#96;./lib&#96;, &#96;./utils&#96;, or under &#96;./src&#96;. Use &#96;--config&#96; for custom path.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### CLI Commands\\\\\\\\n- &#96;npx @better-auth/cli@latest migrate&#96; - Apply schema (built-in adapter)\\\\\\\\n- &#96;npx @better-auth/cli@latest generate&#96; - Generate schema for Prisma/Drizzle\\\\\\\\n- &#96;npx @better-auth/cli mcp --cursor&#96; - Add MCP to AI tools\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Re-run after adding/changing plugins.**\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Core Config Options\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n| Option | Notes |\\\\\\\\n|--------|-------|\\\\\\\\n| &#96;appName&#96; | Optional display name |\\\\\\\\n| &#96;baseURL&#96; | Only if &#96;BETTER_AUTH_URL&#96; not set |\\\\\\\\n| &#96;basePath&#96; | Default &#96;/api/auth&#96;. Set &#96;/&#96; for root. |\\\\\\\\n| &#96;secret&#96; | Only if &#96;BETTER_AUTH_SECRET&#96; not set |\\\\\\\\n| &#96;database&#96; | Required for most features. See adapters docs. |\\\\\\\\n| &#96;secondaryStorage&#96; | Redis/KV for sessions &amp; rate limits |\\\\\\\\n| &#96;emailAndPassword&#96; | &#96;{ enabled: true }&#96; to activate |\\\\\\\\n| &#96;socialProviders&#96; | &#96;{ google: { clientId, clientSecret }, ... }&#96; |\\\\\\\\n| &#96;plugins&#96; | Array of plugins |\\\\\\\\n| &#96;trustedOrigins&#96; | CSRF whitelist |\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Database\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Direct connections:** Pass &#96;pg.Pool&#96;, &#96;mysql2&#96; pool, &#96;better-sqlite3&#96;, or &#96;bun:sqlite&#96; instance.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**ORM adapters:** Import from &#96;better-auth/adapters/drizzle&#96;, &#96;better-auth/adapters/prisma&#96;, &#96;better-auth/adapters/mongodb&#96;.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Critical:** Better Auth uses adapter model names, NOT underlying table names. If Prisma model is &#96;User&#96; mapping to table &#96;users&#96;, use &#96;modelName: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"user\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&#96; (Prisma reference), not &#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"users\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&#96;.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Session Management\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Storage priority:**\\\\\\\\n1. If &#96;secondaryStorage&#96; defined → sessions go there (not DB)\\\\\\\\n2. Set &#96;session.storeSessionInDatabase: true&#96; to also persist to DB\\\\\\\\n3. No database + &#96;cookieCache&#96; → fully stateless mode\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Cookie cache strategies:**\\\\\\\\n- &#96;compact&#96; (default) - Base64url + HMAC. Smallest.\\\\\\\\n- &#96;jwt&#96; - Standard JWT. Readable but signed.\\\\\\\\n- &#96;jwe&#96; - Encrypted. Maximum security.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Key options:** &#96;session.expiresIn&#96; (default 7 days), &#96;session.updateAge&#96; (refresh interval), &#96;session.cookieCache.maxAge&#96;, &#96;session.cookieCache.version&#96; (change to invalidate all sessions).\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## User &amp; Account Config\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**User:** &#96;user.modelName&#96;, &#96;user.fields&#96; (column mapping), &#96;user.additionalFields&#96;, &#96;user.changeEmail.enabled&#96; (disabled by default), &#96;user.deleteUser.enabled&#96; (disabled by default).\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Account:** &#96;account.modelName&#96;, &#96;account.accountLinking.enabled&#96;, &#96;account.storeAccountCookie&#96; (for stateless OAuth).\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Required for registration:** &#96;email&#96; and &#96;name&#96; fields.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Email Flows\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- &#96;emailVerification.sendVerificationEmail&#96; - Must be defined for verification to work\\\\\\\\n- &#96;emailVerification.sendOnSignUp&#96; / &#96;sendOnSignIn&#96; - Auto-send triggers\\\\\\\\n- &#96;emailAndPassword.sendResetPassword&#96; - Password reset email handler\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Security\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**In &#96;advanced&#96;:**\\\\\\\\n- &#96;useSecureCookies&#96; - Force HTTPS cookies\\\\\\\\n- &#96;disableCSRFCheck&#96; - ⚠️ Security risk\\\\\\\\n- &#96;disableOriginCheck&#96; - ⚠️ Security risk  \\\\\\\\n- &#96;crossSubDomainCookies.enabled&#96; - Share cookies across subdomains\\\\\\\\n- &#96;ipAddress.ipAddressHeaders&#96; - Custom IP headers for proxies\\\\\\\\n- &#96;database.generateId&#96; - Custom ID generation or &#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"serial\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&#96;/&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"uuid\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&#96;/&#96;false&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Rate limiting:** &#96;rateLimit.enabled&#96;, &#96;rateLimit.window&#96;, &#96;rateLimit.max&#96;, &#96;rateLimit.storage&#96; (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"memory\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" | \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"database\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" | \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"secondary-storage\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\").\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Hooks\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Endpoint hooks:** &#96;hooks.before&#96; / &#96;hooks.after&#96; - Array of &#96;{ matcher, handler }&#96;. Use &#96;createAuthMiddleware&#96;. Access &#96;ctx.path&#96;, &#96;ctx.context.returned&#96; (after), &#96;ctx.context.session&#96;.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Database hooks:** &#96;databaseHooks.user.create.before/after&#96;, same for &#96;session&#96;, &#96;account&#96;. Useful for adding default values or post-creation actions.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Hook context (&#96;ctx.context&#96;):** &#96;session&#96;, &#96;secret&#96;, &#96;authCookies&#96;, &#96;password.hash()&#96;/&#96;verify()&#96;, &#96;adapter&#96;, &#96;internalAdapter&#96;, &#96;generateId()&#96;, &#96;tables&#96;, &#96;baseURL&#96;.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Plugins\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Import from dedicated paths for tree-shaking:**\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\nimport { twoFactor } from \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"better-auth/plugins/two-factor\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\nNOT &#96;from \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"better-auth/plugins\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&#96;.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Popular plugins:** &#96;twoFactor&#96;, &#96;organization&#96;, &#96;passkey&#96;, &#96;magicLink&#96;, &#96;emailOtp&#96;, &#96;username&#96;, &#96;phoneNumber&#96;, &#96;admin&#96;, &#96;apiKey&#96;, &#96;bearer&#96;, &#96;jwt&#96;, &#96;multiSession&#96;, &#96;sso&#96;, &#96;oauthProvider&#96;, &#96;oidcProvider&#96;, &#96;openAPI&#96;, &#96;genericOAuth&#96;.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nClient plugins go in &#96;createAuthClient({ plugins: [...] })&#96;.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Client\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nImport from: &#96;better-auth/client&#96; (vanilla), &#96;better-auth/react&#96;, &#96;better-auth/vue&#96;, &#96;better-auth/svelte&#96;, &#96;better-auth/solid&#96;.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nKey methods: &#96;signUp.email()&#96;, &#96;signIn.email()&#96;, &#96;signIn.social()&#96;, &#96;signOut()&#96;, &#96;useSession()&#96;, &#96;getSession()&#96;, &#96;revokeSession()&#96;, &#96;revokeSessions()&#96;.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Type Safety\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nInfer types: &#96;typeof auth.$Infer.Session&#96;, &#96;typeof auth.$Infer.Session.user&#96;.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nFor separate client/server projects: &#96;createAuthClient&lt;typeof auth&gt;()&#96;.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Common Gotchas\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n1. **Model vs table name** - Config uses ORM model name, not DB table name\\\\\\\\n2. **Plugin schema** - Re-run CLI after adding plugins\\\\\\\\n3. **Secondary storage** - Sessions go there by default, not DB\\\\\\\\n4. **Cookie cache** - Custom session fields NOT cached, always re-fetched\\\\\\\\n5. **Stateless mode** - No DB = session in cookie only, logout on cache expiry\\\\\\\\n6. **Change email flow** - Sends to current email first, then new email\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Triggers on tasks involving compound components,\\\\\\\\n  render props, context providers, or component architecture. Includes React 19\\\\\\\\n  API changes.\\\\\\\\nlicense: MIT\\\\\\\\nmetadata:\\\\\\\\n  author: vercel\\\\\\\\n  version: '1.0.0'\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n# React Composition Patterns\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nComposition patterns for building flexible, maintainable React components. Avoid\\\\\\\\nboolean prop proliferation by using compound components, lifting state, and\\\\\\\\ncomposing internals. These patterns make codebases easier for both humans and AI\\\\\\\\nagents to work with as they scale.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## When to Apply\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nReference these guidelines when:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- Refactoring components with many boolean props\\\\\\\\n- Building reusable component libraries\\\\\\\\n- Designing flexible component APIs\\\\\\\\n- Reviewing component architecture\\\\\\\\n- Working with compound components or context providers\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Rule Categories by Priority\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n| Priority | Category                | Impact | Prefix          |\\\\\\\\n| -------- | ----------------------- | ------ | --------------- |\\\\\\\\n| 1        | Component Architecture  | HIGH   | &#96;architecture-&#96; |\\\\\\\\n| 2        | State Management        | MEDIUM | &#96;state-&#96;        |\\\\\\\\n| 3        | Implementation Patterns | MEDIUM | &#96;patterns-&#96;     |\\\\\\\\n| 4        | React 19 APIs           | MEDIUM | &#96;react19-&#96;      |\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Quick Reference\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### 1. Component Architecture (HIGH)\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- &#96;architecture-avoid-boolean-props&#96; - Don't add boolean props to customize\\\\\\\\n  behavior; use composition\\\\\\\\n- &#96;architecture-compound-components&#96; - Structure complex components with shared\\\\\\\\n  context\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### 2. State Management (MEDIUM)\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- &#96;state-decouple-implementation&#96; - Provider is the only place that knows how\\\\\\\\n  state is managed\\\\\\\\n- &#96;state-context-interface&#96; - Define generic interface with state, actions, meta\\\\\\\\n  for dependency injection\\\\\\\\n- &#96;state-lift-state&#96; - Move state into provider components for sibling access\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### 3. Implementation Patterns (MEDIUM)\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- &#96;patterns-explicit-variants&#96; - Create explicit variant components instead of\\\\\\\\n  boolean modes\\\\\\\\n- &#96;patterns-children-over-render-props&#96; - Use children for composition instead\\\\\\\\n  of renderX props\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### 4. React 19 APIs (MEDIUM)\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&gt; **⚠️ React 19+ only.** Skip this section if using React 18 or earlier.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- &#96;react19-no-forwardref&#96; - Don't use &#96;forwardRef&#96;; use &#96;use()&#96; instead of &#96;useContext()&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## How to Use\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nRead individual rule files for detailed explanations and code examples:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\nrules/architecture-avoid-boolean-props.md\\\\\\\\nrules/state-context-interface.md\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nEach rule file Authenticate Server Actions Like API Routes\\\\\\\\nimpact: CRITICAL\\\\\\\\nimpactDescription: prevents unauthorized access to server mutations\\\\\\\\ntags: server, server-actions, authentication, security, authorization\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Authenticate Server Actions Like API Routes\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Impact: CRITICAL (prevents unauthorized access to server mutations)**\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nServer Actions (functions with &#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"use server\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&#96;) are exposed as public endpoints, just like API routes. Always verify authentication and authorization **inside** each Server Action—do not rely solely on middleware, layout guards, or page-level checks, as Server Actions can be invoked directly.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nNext.js documentation explicitly states: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Treat Server Actions with the same security considerations as public-facing API endpoints, and verify if the user is allowed to perform a mutation.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Incorrect (no authentication check):**\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\\\\\\\\n'use server'\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nexport async function deleteUser(userId: string) {\\\\\\\\n  // Anyone can call this! No auth check\\\\\\\\n  await db.user.delete({ where: { id: userId } })\\\\\\\\n  return { success: true }\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Correct (authentication inside the action):**\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\\\\\\\\n'use server'\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nimport { verifySession } from '@/lib/auth'\\\\\\\\nimport { unauthorized } from '@/lib/errors'\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nexport async function deleteUser(userId: string) {\\\\\\\\n  // Always check auth inside the action\\\\\\\\n  const session = await verifySession()\\\\\\\\n  \\\\\\\\n  if (!session) {\\\\\\\\n    throw unauthorized('Must be logged in')\\\\\\\\n  }\\\\\\\\n  \\\\\\\\n  // Check authorization too\\\\\\\\n  if (session.user.role !== 'admin' &amp;&amp; session.user.id !== userId) {\\\\\\\\n    throw unauthorized('Cannot delete other users')\\\\\\\\n  }\\\\\\\\n  \\\\\\\\n  await db.user.delete({ where: { id: userId } })\\\\\\\\n  return { success: true }\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**With input validation:**\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\\\\\\\\n'use server'\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nimport { verifySession } from '@/lib/auth'\\\\\\\\nimport { z } from 'zod'\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nconst updateProfileSchema = z.object({\\\\\\\\n  userId: z.string().uuid(),\\\\\\\\n  name: z.string().min(1).max(100),\\\\\\\\n  email: z.string().email()\\\\\\\\n})\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nexport async function updateProfile(data: unknown) {\\\\\\\\n  // Validate input first\\\\\\\\n  const validated = updateProfileSchema.parse(data)\\\\\\\\n  \\\\\\\\n  // Then authenticate\\\\\\\\n  const session = await verifySession()\\\\\\\\n  if (!session) {\\\\\\\\n    throw new Error('Unauthorized')\\\\\\\\n  }\\\\\\\\n  \\\\\\\\n  // Then authorize\\\\\\\\n  if (session.user.id !== validated.userId) {\\\\\\\\n    throw new Error('Can only update own profile')\\\\\\\\n  }\\\\\\\\n  \\\\\\\\n  // Finally perform the mutation\\\\\\\\n  await db.user.update({\\\\\\\\n    where: { id: validated.userId },\\\\\\\\n    data: {\\\\\\\\n      name: validated.name,\\\\\\\\n      email: validated.email\\\\\\\\n    }\\\\\\\\n  })\\\\\\\\n  \\\\\\\\n  return { success: true }\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nReference: [https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/authentication](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/authentication)\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"totalLinesInFile\\\\\\\":97}\\\"},\\\"capabilityType\\\":15}\",\"b0af1992-ce37-42ed-bceb-ef94d25676a9\":\"{\\\"_v\\\":3,\\\"type\\\":2,\\\"approximateLintErrors\\\":[],\\\"lints\\\":[],\\\"codebaseContextChunks\\\":[],\\\"commits\\\":[],\\\"pullRequests\\\":[],\\\"attachedCodeChunks\\\":[],\\\"assistantSuggestedDiffs\\\":[],\\\"gitDiffs\\\":[],\\\"interpreterResults\\\":[],\\\"images\\\":[],\\\"attachedFolders\\\":[],\\\"attachedFoldersNew\\\":[],\\\"bubbleId\\\":\\\"36afe0f4-08e1-435c-a001-bdbe3b3723d9\\\",\\\"userResponsesToSuggestedCodeBlocks\\\":[],\\\"suggestedCodeBlocks\\\":[],\\\"diffsForCompressingFiles\\\":[],\\\"relevantFiles\\\":[],\\\"toolResults\\\":[],\\\"notepads\\\":[],\\\"capabilities\\\":[],\\\"multiFileLinterErrors\\\":[],\\\"diffHistories\\\":[],\\\"recentLocationsHistory\\\":[],\\\"recentlyViewedFiles\\\":[],\\\"isAgentic\\\":false,\\\"fileDiffTrajectories\\\":[],\\\"existedSubsequentTerminalCommand\\\":false,\\\"existedPreviousTerminalCommand\\\":false,\\\"docsReferences\\\":[],\\\"webReferences\\\":[],\\\"aiWebSearchResults\\\":[],\\\"requestId\\\":\\\"\\\",\\\"attachedFoldersListDirResults\\\":[],\\\"humanChanges\\\":[],\\\"attachedHumanChanges\\\":false,\\\"summarizedComposers\\\":[],\\\"cursorRules\\\":[],\\\"contextPieces\\\":[],\\\"editTrailContexts\\\":[],\\\"allThinkingBlocks\\\":[],\\\"diffsSinceLastApply\\\":[],\\\"deletedFiles\\\":[],\\\"supportedTools\\\":[],\\\"tokenCount\\\":{\\\"inputTokens\\\":0,\\\"outputTokens\\\":0},\\\"attachedFileCodeChunksMetadataOnly\\\":[],\\\"consoleLogs\\\":[],\\\"uiElementPicked\\\":[],\\\"isRefunded\\\":false,\\\"knowledgeItems\\\":[],\\\"documentationSelections\\\":[],\\\"externalLinks\\\":[],\\\"projectLayouts\\\":[],\\\"unifiedMode\\\":2,\\\"capabilityContexts\\\":[],\\\"todos\\\":[],\\\"createdAt\\\":\\\"2026-02-15T23:22:18.727Z\\\",\\\"mcpDescriptors\\\":[],\\\"workspaceUris\\\":[],\\\"conversationState\\\":{\\\"rootPromptMessagesJson\\\":[],\\\"turnsOld\\\":[],\\\"todos\\\":[],\\\"pendingToolCalls\\\":[],\\\"turns\\\":[],\\\"previousWorkspaceUris\\\":[],\\\"fileStates\\\":{},\\\"summaryArchives\\\":[],\\\"turnTimings\\\":[],\\\"fileStatesV2\\\":{},\\\"subagentStates\\\":{},\\\"selfSummaryCount\\\":0,\\\"readPaths\\\":[]},\\\"text\\\":\\\"\\\",\\\"toolFormerData\\\":{\\\"toolCallId\\\":\\\"tool_057cd68e-e0a7-4bab-ae87-61173eb1054\\\",\\\"toolIndex\\\":0,\\\"modelCallId\\\":\\\"tool_057cd68e-e0a7-4bab-ae87-61173eb1054\\\",\\\"status\\\":\\\"completed\\\",\\\"name\\\":\\\"read_file_v2\\\",\\\"rawArgs\\\":\\\"{\\\\\\\"path\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"/home/gonzalo/gonzalopozo.dev2/gonzalopozo.github.io/.agents/skills/next-best-practices/error-handling.md\\\\\\\"}\\\",\\\"tool\\\":40,\\\"params\\\":\\\"{\\\\\\\"targetFile\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"/home/gonzalo/gonzalopozo.dev2/gonzalopozo.github.io/.agents/skills/next-best-practices/error-handling.md\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"charsLimit\\\\\\\":1000000,\\\\\\\"effectiveUri\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"/home/gonzalo/gonzalopozo.dev2/gonzalopozo.github.io/.agents/skills/next-best-practices/error-handling.md\\\\\\\"}\\\",\\\"result\\\":\\\"{\\\\\\\"contents\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"# Error Handling\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nHandle errors gracefully in Next.js applications.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nReference: https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/error-handling\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Error Boundaries\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### &#96;error.tsx&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nCatches errors in a route segment and its children:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\\\\\\\\n'use client'\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nexport default function Error({\\\\\\\\n  error,\\\\\\\\n  reset,\\\\\\\\n}: {\\\\\\\\n  error: Error &amp; { digest?: string }\\\\\\\\n  reset: () =&gt; void\\\\\\\\n}) {\\\\\\\\n  return (\\\\\\\\n    &lt;div&gt;\\\\\\\\n      &lt;h2&gt;Something went wrong!&lt;/h2&gt;\\\\\\\\n      &lt;button onClick={() =&gt; reset()}&gt;Try again&lt;/button&gt;\\\\\\\\n    &lt;/div&gt;\\\\\\\\n  )\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Important:** &#96;error.tsx&#96; must be a Client Component.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### &#96;global-error.tsx&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nCatches errors in root layout:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\\\\\\\\n'use client'\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nexport default function GlobalError({\\\\\\\\n  error,\\\\\\\\n  reset,\\\\\\\\n}: {\\\\\\\\n  error: Error &amp; { digest?: string }\\\\\\\\n  reset: () =&gt; void\\\\\\\\n}) {\\\\\\\\n  return (\\\\\\\\n    &lt;html&gt;\\\\\\\\n      &lt;body&gt;\\\\\\\\n        &lt;h2&gt;Something went wrong!&lt;/h2&gt;\\\\\\\\n        &lt;button onClick={() =&gt; reset()}&gt;Try again&lt;/button&gt;\\\\\\\\n      &lt;/body&gt;\\\\\\\\n    &lt;/html&gt;\\\\\\\\n  )\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Important:** Must include &#96;&lt;html&gt;&#96; and &#96;&lt;body&gt;&#96; tags.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Server Actions: Navigation API Gotcha\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Do NOT wrap navigation APIs in try-catch.** They throw special errors that Next.js handles internally.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nReference: https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/redirect#behavior\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\\\\\\\\n'use server'\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nimport { redirect } from 'next/navigation'\\\\\\\\nimport { notFound } from 'next/navigation'\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n// Bad: try-catch catches the navigation \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"error\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\nasync function createPost(formData: FormData) {\\\\\\\\n  try {\\\\\\\\n    const post = await db.post.create({ ... })\\\\\\\\n    redirect(&#96;/posts/${post.id}&#96;)  // This throws!\\\\\\\\n  } catch (error) {\\\\\\\\n    // redirect() throw is caught here - navigation fails!\\\\\\\\n    return { error: 'Failed to create post' }\\\\\\\\n  }\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n// Good: Call navigation APIs outside try-catch\\\\\\\\nasync function createPost(formData: FormData) {\\\\\\\\n  let post\\\\\\\\n  try {\\\\\\\\n    post = await db.post.create({ ... })\\\\\\\\n  } catch (error) {\\\\\\\\n    return { error: 'Failed to create post' }\\\\\\\\n  }\\\\\\\\n  redirect(&#96;/posts/${post.id}&#96;)  // Outside try-catch\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n// Good: Re-throw navigation errors\\\\\\\\nasync function createPost(formData: FormData) {\\\\\\\\n  try {\\\\\\\\n    const post = await db.post.create({ ... })\\\\\\\\n    redirect(&#96;/posts/${post.id}&#96;)\\\\\\\\n  } catch (error) {\\\\\\\\n    if (error instanceof Error &amp;&amp; error.message === 'NEXT_REDIRECT') {\\\\\\\\n      throw error  // Re-throw navigation errors\\\\\\\\n    }\\\\\\\\n    return { error: 'Failed to create post' }\\\\\\\\n  }\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nSame applies to:\\\\\\\\n- &#96;redirect()&#96; - 307 temporary redirect\\\\\\\\n- &#96;permanentRedirect()&#96; - 308 permanent redirect\\\\\\\\n- &#96;notFound()&#96; - 404 not found\\\\\\\\n- &#96;forbidden()&#96; - 403 forbidden\\\\\\\\n- &#96;unauthorized()&#96; - 401 unauthorized\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nUse &#96;unstable_rethrow()&#96; to re-throw these errors in catch blocks:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\\\\\\\\nimport { unstable_rethrow } from 'next/navigation'\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nasync function action() {\\\\\\\\n  try {\\\\\\\\n    // ...\\\\\\\\n    redirect('/success')\\\\\\\\n  } catch (error) {\\\\\\\\n    unstable_rethrow(error) // Re-throws Next.js internal errors\\\\\\\\n    return { error: 'Something went wrong' }\\\\\\\\n  }\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Redirects\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\\\\\\\\nimport { redirect, permanentRedirect } from 'next/navigation'\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n// 307 Temporary - use for most cases\\\\\\\\nredirect('/new-path')\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n// 308 Permanent - use for URL migrations (cached by browsers)\\\\\\\\npermanentRedirect('/new-url')\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Auth Errors\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nTrigger auth-related error pages:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\\\\\\\\nimport { forbidden, unauthorized } from 'next/navigation'\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nasync function Page() {\\\\\\\\n  const session = await getSession()\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n  if (!session) {\\\\\\\\n    unauthorized() // Renders unauthorized.tsx (401)\\\\\\\\n  }\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n  if (!session.hasAccess) {\\\\\\\\n    forbidden() // Renders forbidden.tsx (403)\\\\\\\\n  }\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n  return &lt;Dashboard /&gt;\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nCreate corresponding error pages:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\\\\\\\\n// app/forbidden.tsx\\\\\\\\nexport default function Forbidden() {\\\\\\\\n  return &lt;div&gt;You don't have access to this resource&lt;/div&gt;\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n// app/unauthorized.tsx\\\\\\\\nexport default function Unauthorized() {\\\\\\\\n  return &lt;div&gt;Please log in to continue&lt;/div&gt;\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Not Found\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### &#96;not-found.tsx&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nCustom 404 page for a route segment:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\\\\\\\\nexport default function NotFound() {\\\\\\\\n  return (\\\\\\\\n    &lt;div&gt;\\\\\\\\n      &lt;h2&gt;Not Found&lt;/h2&gt;\\\\\\\\n      &lt;p&gt;Could not find the requested resource&lt;/p&gt;\\\\\\\\n    &lt;/div&gt;\\\\\\\\n  )\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Triggering Not Found\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\\\\\\\\nimport { notFound } from 'next/navigation'\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nexport default async function Page({ params }: { params: Promise&lt;{ id: string }&gt; }) {\\\\\\\\n  const { id } = await params\\\\\\\\n  const post = await getPost(id)\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n  if (!post) {\\\\\\\\n    notFound()  // Renders closest not-found.tsx\\\\\\\\n  }\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n  return &lt;div&gt;{post.title}&lt;/div&gt;\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Error Hierarchy\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nErrors bubble up to the nearest error Route Handlers\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nCreate API endpoints with &#96;route.ts&#96; files.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Basic Usage\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\\\\\\\\n// app/api/users/route.ts\\\\\\\\nexport async function GET() {\\\\\\\\n  const users = await getUsers()\\\\\\\\n  return Response.json(users)\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nexport async function POST(request: Request) {\\\\\\\\n  const body = await request.json()\\\\\\\\n  const user = await createUser(body)\\\\\\\\n  return Response.json(user, { status: 201 })\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Supported Methods\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;GET&#96;, &#96;POST&#96;, &#96;PUT&#96;, &#96;PATCH&#96;, &#96;DELETE&#96;, &#96;HEAD&#96;, &#96;OPTIONS&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## GET Handler Conflicts with page.tsx\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**A &#96;route.ts&#96; and &#96;page.tsx&#96; cannot coexist in the same folder.**\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\napp/\\\\\\\\n├── api/\\\\\\\\n│   └── users/\\\\\\\\n│       └── route.ts    # /api/users\\\\\\\\n└── users/\\\\\\\\n    ├── page.tsx        # /users (page)\\\\\\\\n    └── route.ts        # Warning: Conflicts with page.tsx!\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nIf you need both a page and an API at the same path, use different paths:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\napp/\\\\\\\\n├── users/\\\\\\\\n│   └── page.tsx        # /users (page)\\\\\\\\n└── api/\\\\\\\\n    └── users/\\\\\\\\n        └── route.ts    # /api/users (API)\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Environment Behavior\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nRoute handlers run in a **Server Component-like environment**:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- Yes: Can use &#96;async/await&#96;\\\\\\\\n- Yes: Can access &#96;cookies()&#96;, &#96;headers()&#96;\\\\\\\\n- Yes: Can use Node.js APIs\\\\\\\\n- No: Cannot use React hooks\\\\\\\\n- No: Cannot use React DOM APIs\\\\\\\\n- No: Cannot use browser APIs\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\\\\\\\\n// Bad: This won't work - no React DOM in route handlers\\\\\\\\nimport { renderToString } from 'react-dom/server'\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nexport async function GET() {\\\\\\\\n  const html = renderToString(&lt;Component /&gt;)  // Error!\\\\\\\\n  return new Response(html)\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Dynamic Route Handlers\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\\\\\\\\n// app/api/users/[id]/route.ts\\\\\\\\nexport async function GET(\\\\\\\\n  request: Request,\\\\\\\\n  { params }: { params: Promise&lt;{ id: string }&gt; }\\\\\\\\n) {\\\\\\\\n  const { id } = await params\\\\\\\\n  const user = await getUser(id)\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n  if (!user) {\\\\\\\\n    return Response.json({ error: 'Not found' }, { status: 404 })\\\\\\\\n  }\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n  return Response.json(user)\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Request Helpers\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\\\\\\\\nexport async function GET(request: Request) {\\\\\\\\n  // URL and search params\\\\\\\\n  const { searchParams } = new URL(request.url)\\\\\\\\n  const query = searchParams.get('q')\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n  // Headers\\\\\\\\n  const authHeader = request.headers.get('authorization')\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n  // Cookies (Next.js helper)\\\\\\\\n  const cookieStore = await cookies()\\\\\\\\n  const token = cookieStore.get('token')\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n  return Response.json({ query, token })\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Response Helpers\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\\\\\\\\n// JSON response\\\\\\\\nreturn Response.json({ data })\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n// With status\\\\\\\\nreturn Response.json({ error: 'Not found' }, { status: 404 })\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n// With headers\\\\\\\\nreturn Response.json(data, {\\\\\\\\n  headers: {\\\\\\\\n    'Cache-Control': 'max-age=3600',\\\\\\\\n  },\\\\\\\\n})\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n// Redirect\\\\\\\\nreturn Response.redirect(new },\\\\\\\\n})\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## When to Use Route Handlers vs Server Actions\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n| Use Case | Route Handlers | Server Actions |\\\\\\\\n|----------|----------------|----------------|\\\\\\\\n| Form submissions | No | Yes |\\\\\\\\n| Data mutations from UI | No | Yes |\\\\\\\\n| Third-party webhooks | Yes | No |\\\\\\\\n| External API consumption | Yes | No |\\\\\\\\n| Public REST API | Yes | No |\\\\\\\\n| File uploads | Both work | Both work |\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Prefer Server Actions** for mutations triggered from ## Security Audit Results

### What's already covered (by AGENTS.md + installed skills)

| Topic | Where Covered | Coverage Level |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **CSRF Protection** | `better-auth-best-practices` skill (`trustedOrigins`, SameSite cookies) | Good — better-auth handles CSRF automatically |
| **Secure Cookies & Sessions** | `better-auth-best-practices` skill (`useSecureCookies`, cookie cache strategies) + AGENTS.md mentions HTTP-only secure settings | Good — better-auth manages this |
| **SQL Injection Prevention** | `drizzle-orm` skill (parameterized queries, `sql` template warning) | Good — Drizzle ORM handles parameterized queries |
| **Server Actions Security** | `vercel-react-best-practices` skill (auth + authorization inside Server Actions, Zod validation) + `next-best-practices` skill (`unauthorized()`, `forbidden()`) | Good — covered by two skills |
| **Input Validation (Zod)** | `vercel-react-best-practices` skill (Zod schema examples) + AGENTS.md Server Actions Pattern mentions "coming soon: Zod schema validation" | Partial — principles covered, project-specific patterns not documented |
| **Environment Variables** | AGENTS.md mentions `.env.local` and `TURSO_AUTH_TOKEN` + `better-auth-best-practices` covers `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` | Partial — basics covered, Vercel sensitive vars and classification rules not documented |
| **Auth Protection via proxy.ts** | Your `proxy.ts` already uses cookie-based optimistic redirects, matching the better-auth recommended pattern | Partial — implemented in code, not documented in AGENTS.md |

### What's NOT covered (gaps)

| Topic | Gap | Severity |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Content Security Policy (CSP)** | No CSP implementation documented or in code. No nonce generation, no CSP headers. None of the installed skills cover CSP. | **High** — XSS is the most common web vulnerability |
| **Security Headers** | No `headers()` config in `next.config.ts`. Missing HSTS, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy | **High** — basic hardening, easy to implement |
| **Input Sanitization (HTML/DOMPurify)** | Zod validation is planned but HTML sanitization for rich content is not covered. Your project stores `description` fields that could contain user input. | **Medium** — relevant if descriptions ever accept HTML |
| **Dependency Security** | No `pnpm audit` workflow, no npm-check-updates script, no documentation on keeping deps updated | **Medium** — important for ongoing maintenance |
| **Source Maps Security** | `productionBrowserSourceMaps` not explicitly set. Default is `false` in Next.js (safe), but not documented as an explicit decision | **Low** — safe by default, but should be documented |
| **Vercel Security Features** | No documentation on Vercel Firewall, DDoS protection, sensitive environment variables, or deployment security | **Low** — Vercel provides these automatically, but documenting the project's approach is useful |
| **Fundamental Security Principles** | No Defense in Depth, Least Privilege, or Keep Updated principles documented | **Low** — good to have as a reference for the developer mindset |
| **Auth pattern in proxy.ts** | Current implementation uses cookie check only (correct per better-auth docs), but the reasoning and security implications aren't documented | **Low** — implemented correctly, just needs documentation |

### Summary

Your project has **good foundational security** through better-auth (CSRF, sessions, cookies), Drizzle ORM (SQL injection), and the Server Action skills (auth + Zod validation). The main gaps are:

1. **CSP** — no implementation at all (high impact)
2. **Security Headers** — not configured in `next.config.ts` (high impact, easy fix)
3. **Input Sanitization** — Zod planned but HTML sanitization not covered
4. **Dependency Auditing** — no workflow documented
5. **Source Maps / Vercel / Principles** — documentation gaps

Given the volume of gaps, I recommend the same approach we used for Performance and Accessibility: create a sub `AGENTS-SECURITY.md` to cover all project-specific security patterns that aren't handled by the existing skills.

Security
Security is fundamental in modern web applications. This guide provides practical examples and proven patterns to protect your Next.js application deployed on Vercel, based on official documentation and industry best practices.

Content Security Policy (CSP) (https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/content-security-policy):
CSP is essential to protect against XSS attacks, clickjacking, and code injection. Implement CSP with nonces in Next.js for enhanced security.
CSP Implementation with Proxy example:
import { NextResponse } from 'next/server';

export function proxy(request) {
  // Generate unique nonce for each request
  const nonce = Buffer.from(crypto.randomUUID()).toString('base64');
  const isDev = process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development';

  const cspHeader = `
    default-src 'self';
    script-src 'self' 'nonce-${nonce}' 'strict-dynamic' ${isDev ? "'unsafe-eval'" : ''};
    style-src 'self' ${isDev ? "'unsafe-inline'" : `'nonce-${nonce}'`};
    img-src 'self' blob: data: https:;
    font-src 'self';
    object-src 'none';
    base-uri 'self';
    form-action 'self';
    frame-ancestors 'none';
    upgrade-insecure-requests;
  `;

  const contentSecurityPolicyHeaderValue = cspHeader
    .replace(/\s{2,}/g, ' ')
    .trim();

  const requestHeaders = new Headers(request.headers);
  requestHeaders.set('x-nonce', nonce);
  requestHeaders.set('Content-Security-Policy', contentSecurityPolicyHeaderValue);

  const response = NextResponse.next({
    request: { headers: requestHeaders },
  });
  
  response.headers.set('Content-Security-Policy', contentSecurityPolicyHeaderValue);
  return response;
}

export const config = {
  matcher: [
    {
      source: '/((?!api|_next/static|_next/image|favicon.ico).*)',
      missing: [
        { type: 'header', key: 'next-router-prefetch' },
        { type: 'header', key: 'purpose', value: 'prefetch' },
      ],
    },
  ],
};

Secure Environment Variables (https://vercel.com/docs/environment-variables/sensitive-environment-variables):
Handle secrets and credentials securely with environment variables. Vercel offers encrypted sensitive variables that are never exposed.
Variables Configuration example:
# Database credentials - NEVER commit to git
DATABASE_URL="postgresql://user:password@localhost:5432/mydb"

# API Keys - Use Vercel's sensitive environment variables
STRIPE_SECRET_KEY="sk_live_..."
OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-..."

# Public variables (can be exposed to browser)
NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL="https://api.example.com"

# Auth secrets - Generate with: openssl rand -base64 32
NEXTAUTH_SECRET="your-secret-here"
NEXTAUTH_URL="https://yourdomain.com"

# Vercel automatically provides these:
# VERCEL_URL - Deployment URL
# VERCEL_ENV - Environment (production, preview, development)

Better-auth & proxy.ts Next.js 16 approach:
Handle auth checks in each page/route. Do not use @proxy.ts do to auth checks, just for optimistically redirect users like we do in this project. Just as better-auth tell in it's documentation https://www.better-auth.com/docs/integrations/next#auth-protection.

Input Sanitization & Validation (https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Input_Validation_Cheat_Sheet.html):
Validate and sanitize all user inputs. Use validation schemas and sanitize HTML to prevent XSS attacks.
Validation with Zod & DOMPurify example:
import { NextResponse } from 'next/server';
import DOMPurify from 'isomorphic-dompurify';
import { z } from 'zod';

// Validation schema
const PostSchema = z.object({
  title: z.string().min(1).max(200),
  content: z.string().min(1).max(10000),
  authorId: z.string().uuid(),
});

export async function POST(request) {
  try {
    const body = await request.json();
    
    // Validate input
    const validatedData = PostSchema.parse(body);
    
    // Sanitize HTML content to prevent XSS
    const sanitizedContent = DOMPurify.sanitize(validatedData.content, {
      ALLOWED_TAGS: ['p', 'br', 'strong', 'em', 'a'],
      ALLOWED_ATTR: ['href'],
    });
    
    // Save to database with parameterized queries
    const post = await db.post.create({
      data: {
        title: validatedData.title,
        content: sanitizedContent,
        authorId: validatedData.authorId,
      },
    });
    
    return NextResponse.json(post, { status: 201 });
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof z.ZodError) {
      return NextResponse.json(
        { error: 'Invalid input', details: error.errors },
        { status: 400 }
      );
    }
    
    // Don't expose internal errors
    console.error('Post creation error:', error);
    return NextResponse.json(
      { error: 'Internal server error' },
      { status: 500 }
    );
  }
}

Vercel Security Features (https://vercel.com/docs/security):
Vercel provides multiple security layers: Firewall, DDoS protection, encrypted sensitive variables, and automatic HTTPS on all deployments.
Vercel Configuration example:
# Install Vercel CLI
npm i -g vercel

# Set sensitive environment variables via CLI
vercel env add DATABASE_URL
# Select environment: Production, Preview, Development
# Type: sensitive (encrypted and non-readable)

# Configure Vercel Firewall (Enterprise)
# Enable firewall protection against common attacks:
# - SQL Injection
# - Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
# - Scanner Detection
# - Local File Inclusion (LFI)

# View deployment logs for security monitoring
vercel logs <deployment-url>

# Enable Attack Challenge Mode
# Go to: Project Settings > Security > Attack Challenge Mode

CSRF Protection (https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Cross-Site_Request_Forgery_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html):
Protect against Cross-Site Request Forgery attacks using CSRF tokens. Verify the authenticity of each request that modifies data.
CSRF Tokens Implementation example: 
import { NextResponse } from 'next/server';
import { randomBytes } from 'crypto';

// Generate CSRF token
export async function GET() {
  const token = randomBytes(32).toString('hex');
  
  const response = NextResponse.json({ csrfToken: token });
  
  // Set CSRF token in httpOnly cookie
  response.cookies.set('csrf-token', token, {
    httpOnly: true,
    secure: process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production',
    sameSite: 'strict',
    maxAge: 3600, // 1 hour
  });
  
  return response;
}

Dependency Security (https://www.npmjs.com/package/npm-check-updates, https://pnpm.io/cli/audit & https://pnpm.io/cli/update):
Keep your dependencies updated and free from vulnerabilities. Use pnpm audit, Snyk, or Dependabot to detect and fix issues.
Package.json scripts dependency audit example:
"scripts": {
    "dev": "next dev",
    "build": "next build",
    "start": "next start",
    "audit": "pnpm audit",
    "audit:fix": "pnpm audit --fix",
    "check-updates:ncu": "pnpm dlx npm-check-updates",
    "check-updates:pnpm": "pnpm up --latest"
  }

Secure Cookies & Sessions (https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Session_Management_Cheat_Sheet.html):
Configure cookies with security flags. Use httpOnly, secure, and sameSite to protect against XSS and CSRF.
Secure Cookies Configuration example:
import { NextResponse } from 'next/server';

export async function POST(request) {
  const response = NextResponse.json({ success: true });
  
  // Secure cookie configuration
  response.cookies.set('session', 'your-session-token', {
    httpOnly: true,        // Prevents JavaScript access
    secure: true,          // Only sent over HTTPS
    sameSite: 'strict',    // CSRF protection
    maxAge: 60 * 60 * 24,  // 1 day
    path: '/',
  });
  
  return response;
}

SQL Injection Prevention (https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/SQL_Injection_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html):
Use drizzle ORM to prevent SQL injection. Never concatenate strings directly in queries.

Security Headers (https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/headers):
Configure security headers in next.config.js. Include HSTS, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, and Referrer-Policy.
next.config.js with Security Headers example:
/** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */
const nextConfig = {
  reactStrictMode: true,
  
  async headers() {
    return [
      {
        source: '/:path*',
        headers: [
          {
            key: 'X-DNS-Prefetch-Control',
            value: 'on'
          },
          {
            key: 'Strict-Transport-Security',
            value: 'max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload'
          },
          {
            key: 'X-Frame-Options',
            value: 'SAMEORIGIN'
          },
          {
            key: 'X-Content-Type-Options',
            value: 'nosniff'
          },
          {
            key: 'X-XSS-Protection',
            value: '1; mode=block'
          },
          {
            key: 'Referrer-Policy',
            value: 'strict-origin-when-cross-origin'
          },
          {
            key: 'Permissions-Policy',
            value: 'camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()'
          }
        ],
      },
    ];
  },
  
  images: {
    remotePatterns: [
      {
        protocol: 'https',
        hostname: 'trusted-cdn.com',
      },
    ],
  },
};

module.exports = nextConfig;

Server Actions Security (https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/updating-data):
Server Actions must validate authentication and authorization. Always validate inputs and verify user permissions.
Secure Server Action example (this is an example, it won't propably fit as 100% as my project workflow):
'use server';

import { revalidatePath } from 'next/cache';
import { getSession } from '@/lib/session';
import { z } from 'zod';

const UpdateProfileSchema = z.object({
  name: z.string().min(1).max(100),
  bio: z.string().max(500).optional(),
});

export async function updateProfile(formData) {
  // 1. Verify authentication
  const session = await getSession();
  if (!session?.userId) {
    throw new Error('Unauthorized');
  }
  
  // 2. Validate input
  const rawData = {
    name: formData.get('name'),
    bio: formData.get('bio'),
  };
  
  const validatedData = UpdateProfileSchema.parse(rawData);
  
  // 3. Check authorization
  const user = await db.user.findUnique({
    where: { id: session.userId },
  });
  
  if (!user) {
    throw new Error('User not found');
  }
  
  // 4. Perform action
  await db.user.update({
    where: { id: session.userId },
    data: validatedData,
  });
  
  // 5. Revalidate cache
  revalidatePath('/profile');
  
  return { success: true };
}

Source Maps Security (https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/productionBrowserSourceMaps):
Disable source maps in production to prevent exposing your original source code. Source maps reveal your application's internal structure and logic, making it easier for attackers to find vulnerabilities.
Disable Source Maps in Production example:
/** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */
const nextConfig = {
  reactStrictMode: true,
  
  // Disable source maps in production
  productionBrowserSourceMaps: false,
  
  // Additional security configurations
  compiler: {
    // Remove console logs in production
    removeConsole: process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production' ? {
      exclude: ['error', 'warn'],
    } : false,
  },
  
  webpack: (config, { dev, isServer }) => {
    if (!dev && !isServer) {
      // Disable source maps for client-side production builds
      config.devtool = false;
    }
    
    return config;
  },
};

module.exports = nextConfig;

Fundamental Security Principles
1. Defense in Depth
Multiple security layers to protect the application
• Implement CSP, CSRF, and rate limiting

• Use multiple authentication methods

• Validate on both client and server

• Monitor logs and set up alerts

2. Least Privilege
Grant only the minimum permissions necessary
• Users only access what they need

• APIs and services with limited permissions

• Environment variables only where required

• Review permissions regularly

3. Input Validation
Never trust user data
• Validate and sanitize all inputs

• Use validation schemas (Zod, Yup)

• Implement HTML sanitization

• Prevent SQL injection and XSS

4. Keep it Updated
Keep everything updated and monitored
• Update dependencies regularly

• Use audit tools (npm audit, Snyk)

• Apply security patches quickly

• Monitor known vulnerabilities

There's the issue: **`.agents` is in your `.gitignore`**, which means the skills directory will NOT be committed and will NOT be on your laptop tomorrow.

You have two options:

**Option A: Remove `.agents` from `.gitignore` and commit the skills**

This is the simplest approach. The skills are just markdown files (`.md`), so they're small and safe to commit. After removing the line from `.gitignore`, the `.agents/skills/` directory will be part of your repo and available on any machine you clone/pull to.

**Option B: Reinstall skills on your laptop**

Keep `.agents` in `.gitignore` and reinstall all 16 skills on your laptop using:

```bash
pnpm dlx skills add vercel-labs/skills@find-skills -y
pnpm dlx skills add nicepkg/nice-skills@tailwind-v4-shadcn -y
pnpm dlx skills add nicepkg/nice-skills@shadcn-ui -y
pnpm dlx skills add nicepkg/nice-skills@typescript-advanced-types -y
pnpm dlx skills add nicepkg/nice-skills@drizzle-orm -y
pnpm dlx skills add nicepkg/nice-skills@better-auth-best-practices -y
pnpm dlx skills add nicepkg/nice-skills@nextjs-app-router-patterns -y
pnpm dlx skills add nicepkg/nice-skills@frontend-design -y
pnpm dlx skills add nicepkg/nice-skills@web-design-guidelines -y
pnpm dlx skills add nicepkg/nice-skills@vercel-react-best-practices -y
pnpm dlx skills add vercel-labs/next-skills@next-best-practices -y
pnpm dlx skills add vercel-labs/next-skills@next-cache-components -y
pnpm dlx skills add vercel-labs/agent-skills@vercel-composition-patterns -y
pnpm dlx skills add addyosmani/web-quality-skills@seo -y
pnpm dlx skills add addyosmani/web-quality-skills@accessibility -y
pnpm dlx skills add wshobson/agents@wcag-audit-patterns -y
```

**My recommendation: Option A.** Skills are just markdown files — there's no reason to exclude them from git. They're part of your project's AI configuration, just like `AGENTS.md`. Remove the `.agents` line from `.gitignore`, commit everything, and the skills will be on your laptop when you pull.

Your `AGENTS.md`, `AGENTS-PERFORMANCE.md`, `AGENTS-ACCESSIBILITY.md`, `AGENTS-ANIMATIONS.md`, and `AGENTS-SECURITY.md` are already tracked by git (not in `.gitignore`), so those will work on your laptop regardless.
